purpose: Methenamine mandelate is used to prevent or treat urinary tract infections (UTIs). It works best for long-term prevention in people who get UTIs frequently. Your doctor may prescribe it to keep bacteria from growing in your urinary tract.
how_it_works: When this medicine reaches your bladder, it breaks down into a substance called formaldehyde, which kills the bacteria causing the infection. The mandelate part helps make your urine more acidic, which helps the medicine work better. Basically, it turns your urine into an environment where bacteria cannot survive.
common_side_effects: You might notice an upset stomach, nausea, or stomach cramps. Some people experience bladder irritation, which can feel like a burning sensation when urinating or needing to go to the bathroom more often. A skin rash can occasionally occur as well.
warnings: Drink plenty of fluids while taking this medicine, but avoid antacids and alkaline foods like citrus juices, as they can stop the medicine from working properly. Do not take this medicine if you have kidney problems or liver disease, as it may not be safe for you. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, since some drugs can interfere with this one. If you develop a severe rash, difficulty breathing, or signs of a serious allergic reaction, seek medical help right away.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 1 gram taken by mouth four times a day, after meals and at bedtime. Your doctor may adjust your dose depending on your specific situation. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes, and try to take it with food to reduce stomach upset.
